sutta: Now, Sutta 11.7, venerable Ananda came to see the exalted one, paid homage to exalted one and sat down to one side, huh? Then he asked the Buddha, he said, "Please, sir, may it be that among winning of concentration is of such a sort that in earth he is unperceptive of earth, in water unperceptive of water, in fire unperceptive of fire, in air unperceptive of air, in the realm of unbounded space unperceptive of it, in the realm of unbounded, uh, consciousness unperceptive of it, in the realm of nothingness unperceptive of it, in the realm of neither perception nor non-perception also unperceptive of it. That in this world he is unaware of this, unperceptive of this world. In the world beyond he is unperceptive of the world beyond. That whatsoever is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, attained, sought after, thought over by mind of all that he is unperceptive, and yet he perceives." And the Buddha said, "It may be so, Ananda. Among winning of concentration may be of such a sort that in earth he is unperceptive of earth, etc., etc." Then, remember Ananda asked, "But, sir, in what way may a monk's winning of concentration be of such a sort that of all that he is unperceptive, and yet he is perceptive he perceives?" And then the Buddha said, "Herein, Ananda, a monk is conscious thus. This is the real, this is the best, namely the calming of all conditioners, the rejection of every substrate, the ending of craving, the fading of interest, stopping any or cessation any bana." In such way, Ananda, a monk's winning of concentration may be of such a sort that in earth he is unperceptive of earth, etc. That in whatsoever is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, attained, sought after, thought out by mind, of all that he is unperceptive, and yet at the same time he perceives." And that's the end of the sutta. It's quite an interesting sutta. Here, the remember Ananda is asking, "Uh, can a monk, uh, attain a state of concentration, uh, such that, uh, he is in this world, and yet, uh, he is not perceptive of this world?" Usually, the Buddha talks about feeling and perception. Uh, if a person has feeling and perception, uh, it means he has consciousness, uh. He is conscious, uh. So, if a person, uh, has no perception, it also means he has no consciousness, uh. But, this in this case, the Buddha is talking about a person, uh, who has attained a state of concentration that he is not aware of this world at all. He's not aware of He's aware of whatever is seen, sensed, heard, recognized, thought over, etc. And yet now at the same time he is conscious. So, the Buddha said it is possible. It is possible. And he can attain this stage uh when he calms down all his conditioners uh and he has is he is disenchanted with everything in this world uh and he attains cessation. And here he even sees Nibbana. Uh So, here basically what is being said now is that this state of Nibbana is of this sort. If a person attains Nibbana, the six consciousness will stop working. Six consciousness will stop working. And yet there appears to be another type of consciousness. Another type of consciousness where that person is not even aware of himself. The Buddha said, "Monks, 11 advantages are to be looked for from the radiation by mind of loving-kindness, by making the loving-kindness grow, by making much of it, by making loving-kindness a vehicle and basis, by persisting in it, by becoming familiar with it, by well-establishing it. What are the 11? One sleeps happy and wakes happy. He dreams no evil dream. He is dear to human beings and non-human beings alike. The devas or heavenly beings guard him. Fire, poison, or sword affect him not. Quickly, he concentrates his mind. His complexion is serene. He makes an end or he dies without bewilderment. It means unconfused. And if he has penetrated no further, he reaches, upon dying, the Brahma world. These 11 advantages are to be looked for from the radiation by mind of loving-kindness, by making loving-kindness grow, by making much of it, by making loving-kindness a vehicle and basis, by persisting in it, by becoming familiar with it, by well-establishing it. That's the end of the sutta. Here I have translated this uh radiation by mind of loving-kindness.
